## Summary

The rsyslog GitHub repository previously contained an issue auto-labeler workflow that interpolated issue title and body data directly into a shell script. A user able to open an issue could potentially cause command execution in the GitHub Actions runner. The workflow has been removed.

## Affected component

rsyslog GitHub repository automation only: `.github/workflows/label-issues.yml`

## Affected period

2025-06-10 through 2026-05-04

## Impact

This affected the GitHub Actions environment for the rsyslog repository. Potential impact was limited to the workflow runner, possible exposure of the `GEMINI_API_KEY` used by that workflow, and abuse of the workflow's `issues: write` GitHub token permissions.

## Non-impact

This did not affect rsyslog runtime code, rsyslog packages, official release artifacts, or users running rsyslog. GitHub-generated source archives or forks may have contained the workflow file, but the file is only active when used as a GitHub Actions workflow in a repository.

## Resolution

The workflow was removed on 2026-05-04 in commit `8fbac4b3416314d3ada9428b98a6eb6354167ff0`. Forks that copied and enabled this workflow should remove it or update it to pass untrusted GitHub context through environment variables rather than interpolating it directly into shell code.

## CVE

We do not request a CVE because the issue is scoped to GitHub repository automation and does not affect the rsyslog software product or its runtime/distribution artifacts.
